operator_io_quirks: Table/column names are mixed-case (groupName, totalSnatched, groupYear, releaseType, groupId) and one column is a SQL keyword: tags."index" — must be double-quoted everywhere.
tags."index" is a quoted reserved word; upstream upper-cases columns and lower-cases tables, so case-insensitive lookup must still match "index".
FK tags.id -> torrents.id with parent_col NULL (same-name rule); parent torrents.id is a single-column PK, so parent is unique and exists.
tags.id is NOT unique (59853 distinct over 161283 rows) — many child rows share a parent; FK fill draws with replacement, fine.
torrents.groupId is distinct=75719 (== row count) but is NOT declared unique/PK — looks like a natural key; TS will not treat it as one.
torrents.id PK values are 0..N-1 dense integers; tags."index" PK also 0..N-1 — Number fuzzer fresh draws will collide with existing PKs and get dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0 — no NULLs in original, but TS may emit NULLs (String/Number dropout) and inserts will succeed since NOT NULL is not enforced.
groupName/artist contain HTML entities (') and slashes — String fuzzer's CHARSET lacks these, so fresh strings look unlike originals.
groupYear is INTEGER storing years 1979..1983 (38 distinct) — declared INTEGER dispatches to Number, not Date/Year; TS will emit huge ints, not plausible years.
totalSnatched INTEGER with 2816 distinct small ints (109..480) — Number fuzzer range is [-10^scale,10^scale] with default scale, so fresh values are wildly out of range.
releaseType TEXT with 15 distinct enum-like values (single, album, live album, ep, unknown) — String fuzzer will not respect the enum.
Two tables, 75719 and 161283 rows — under max_rows_per_table=300000, so full read; no rowid sampling needed.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer for groupName, artist, releaseType, tag: fresh strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with contamination — implausible vs real titles/artists/tags (FN driver: queries filtering on real artist names or tag values find nothing).

Number fuzzer for totalSnatched, groupYear, groupId, id, "index": fresh draws uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale from type args, default large) — groupYear gets values like 5000000, totalSnatched gets negatives (FN driver: range predicates on year/snatches).
Number fuzzer's list_max quirk (upper end overwritten with full-range max) means even 'element-based' draws can exceed observed max — inflates implausible values.
PK columns id and "index" are single-column PKs -> max_l0 = inf, so fresh draws never reuse; dense 0..N-1 originals mean many fresh PKs collide and rows get dropped, shrinking tables unpredictably.
tags.id FK draws from torrents.id final values with replacement — duplicates in child are expected and correct; joins torrents-tags will have many-to-one fan-out (FP driver if gold expects 1:1).
groupId is not declared unique, so TS may emit duplicate groupIds across torrents rows — queries doing COUNT(DISTINCT groupId) or grouping by groupId see different cardinalities (FP/FN driver).
releaseType enum not respected: fresh strings break WHERE releaseType='single' style predicates (FN driver).
groupYear as Number not Date: no year-template formatting, so BETWEEN 1979 AND 1983 style predicates mostly return empty (FN driver).
No NULLs in original but TS String/Number dropout (0.9 keep) plus p=0.2 fresh can yield NULLs — IS NULL predicates flip from empty to non-empty (FP driver).
HTML entities and slashes in groupName/artist are never reproduced by CHARSET — LIKE '%'%' or exact-match predicates miss (FN driver).

Small tables (2 tables) and shallow FK graph: table order is [torrents] then [tags]; sizes from choose_table_sizes (30..2500 or level-based) — instances are small, so ties/duplicates are common (FP driver for DISTINCT/COUNT).
No CHECK constraints, no unique indexes beyond PKs — drop_unique_duplicates only filters PK duplicates; no other dedup pressure.
